mekki-muskil:103-103.t: His saying {بالأخسرين أعمالا}: أعمالا is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).

mekki-muskil:108-108.t: His saying {عَنْهَا حولا}: it is accusative by يبغون, i.e. a moving away (متحولا). One says حال من يحول حولا when one moves away from it.

mekki-muskil:59-59.t:
His saying {وَتلك الْقرى أهلكناهم}: تِلْكَ is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject), and أهلكناهم is the khabar (predicate). If you wish, تِلْكَ may be in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by an implied (muḍmar) verb which أهلكناهم explains.
His saying {لمهلكهم}: whoever reads it with fatḥa on the lām and the mīm makes it the maṣdar (verbal noun) of هَلَكُوا مهْلكا, and it is annexed (muḍāf) to the object, according to the dialect of those who allow هلك to be transitive; for whoever does not allow it to be transitive, it is annexed to the agent. Whoever reads it with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the lām makes it a noun of time, its implied form being "for the time of their destruction" (لوقت مهلكهم); and it is also said to be a maṣdar of هلك that came irregularly, like الْمرجع and الْمَحيض. Whoever reads it with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the lām makes it the maṣdar of أهلكوا (they were destroyed).

mekki-muskil:61-61.t: His saying {سربا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun); and it is said to be the second object of اتخذ.

mekki-muskil:63-63.t:
His saying {وَمَا أنسانيه إِلَّا الشَّيْطَان أَن أذكرهُ}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ in أنسانيه, and it is a substitute of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).
And His saying {فِي الْبَحْر عجبا}: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) if you make it part of the speech of Mūsā (peace be upon him), and you pause on الْبَحْر; it is as though, when the young man of Mūsā said «and it took its way into the sea» (وَاتخذ سَبيله فِي الْبَحْر), Mūsā said: "I marvel a marvelling" (أعجب عجبا). If you make عجبا part of the speech of Mūsā's young man, it is the second object of اتخذ. It is also said that it is all from the speech of Mūsā (peace be upon him), its implied form being "and Mūsā took the way of the fish into the sea, marvelling a marvelling" (وَاتخذ مُوسَى سَبِيل الْحُوت فِي الْبَحْر تعجب عجبا); so pausing on عجبا according to this interpretation is good.

mekki-muskil:64-64.t: His saying {قصصا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. they both went back following the track, a following (يقصان الْأَثر قصصا).

mekki-muskil:66-66.t: His saying {علمت رشدا}: رشدا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); its meaning is "May I follow you for the sake of right guidance, on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught?", so that على and what follows it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It may also be the object of تعلمني, its implied form being "on condition that you teach me a matter possessing right guidance" (على أَن تعلمني أمرا ذَا رشد). الرُّشْد and الرَّشَد are two dialectal forms.

mekki-muskil:68-68.t: His saying {تحط بِهِ خَبرا}: خَبرا is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of تحط بِهِ is "you have knowledge of it / are informed of it" (تخبره).

mekki-muskil:77-77.t: His saying {لاتخذت}: whoever reads the tāʾ light (without doubling) takes it from تخذت, and enters the lām that answers لو onto the tāʾ that is the first radical (fāʾ al-fiʿl) of the verb. The lexicographers report تخذت أَتَّخِذ, and Sībawayh reports استخذ فلَان أَرضًا ("so-and-so took land"), whose origin is اتخذ on the pattern افتعل, except that the first tāʾ was replaced by a sīn. Whoever reads it doubled makes it افتعل and assimilates the radical tāʾ into the augment tāʾ. Al-Akhfash said: the first tāʾ in اتخذ is a substitute for a wāw, and the wāw is a substitute for a hamza; and it is said: a substitute for a yāʾ, and the yāʾ a substitute for a hamza — Ibn Kaysān reported this from him.

mekki-muskil:86-86.t:
His saying {تغرب فِي عين}: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in وجدهَا.
His saying {إِمَّا أَن تعذب وَإِمَّا أَن تتَّخذ فيهم}: أَن is in the position of the accusative in both; and it is said to be in the position of the nominative, which is clearer, on the sense of "as for it, it is …" (فَأَما هُوَ), as the poet said:
... فسيرا فَأَما حَاجَة تقضيانها ... وَإِمَّا مقيل صَالح وصديق ...
(So go on, the two of you: either a need you fulfil, or a good resting place and a friend.)
The nominative is by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), and the accusative is by an implied verb, i.e. "either you do the punishing" (فَأَما تفعل أَن تعذب), meaning "you carry out the punishment".

mekki-muskil:88-88.t: His saying {فَلهُ جَزَاء الْحسنى}: whoever reads جَزَاء in the nominative makes it a mubtadaʾ (subject) and له the khabar (predicate); its implied form is "for him is the reward of the best qualities" (فَلهُ جَزَاء الْخلال الْحسنى), so الْحسنى is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) through the annexation of الْجَزَاء to it. It is also said to be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from جَزَاء, the tanwīn having been dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and الْحسنى on this view is Paradise, as though He said "for him is Paradise". Whoever reads جَزَاء in the accusative with tanwīn makes الْحسنى the mubtadaʾ and له the khabar, and جَزَاء is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being "for him are the [best] qualities as a reward" or "Paradise as a reward", i.e. being rewarded with it. It is also said that جَزَاء is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and it is said: as a maṣdar. Whoever reads it in the accusative without tanwīn has only dropped the tanwīn because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and الْحسنى is in the position of the nominative; and there is remoteness (improbability) in this.

mekki-muskil:93-93.t: His saying {لَا يكادون يفقهُونَ}: whoever reads it with ḍamma on the yāʾ (يُفقِهون) assumes an omitted object, its implied form being "they can scarcely make anyone understand speech" (لَا يفقهُونَ أحدا قولا); and there is no omission with fatḥa on the yāʾ.

mekki-muskil:94-94.t: His saying {يَأْجُوج وَمَأْجُوج}: they are diptotes (not fully declined) because they are two names of two tribes, together with definiteness; and it is said: together with foreignness (ʿujma). Whoever pronounces them with hamza makes them Arabic, derived from أجيج النار (the blazing of fire), and from that is His saying مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ ("salty and bitter"); so they are on the patterns يفعول and مفعول. It is also possible that whoever does not pronounce the hamza intends the hamza but lightened it, so that it is Arabic as well.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {سِنِين}: accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and {عددا} is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It has also been said it is a naʿt (adjective) of سنين in the sense of "possessing number". Al-Farrāʾ said its meaning is "counted (معدودة)", so on this view it is a naʿt of سنين.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying {أحصى لما لَبِثُوا أمدا}: أمدا is accusative because it is the object of أحصى, as though He said: so that We may know whether these or those reckoned the term better [Translator's note: literally "whether these have reckoned the term or those"]. It has also been said it is accusative by لبثوا. Al-Zajjāj permitted making it accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and others disallowed it, because if one makes it accusative as a tamyīz, one makes أحصى a noun on the pattern afʿal (the elative), whereas أحصى is originally the form of the past from أحصى يحصي; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said أَحْصَاهُ الله ونسوه and وأحصى كل شَيْء عددا. If it is established that it occurs as a past verb, it is impossible to use from it [the form] afʿal min kadhā ("more … than"); afʿal min kadhā always comes from the triliteral and never from the quadriliteral, except anomalously, as in their saying مَا أولاه للخير ("how given he is to good!") and مَا أعطَاهُ للدرهم ("how generous he is with the dirham!"), which is anomalous and not taken as a basis for analogy. Since afʿal min kadhā cannot come from the quadriliteral, it is known that أحصى is not afʿal min kadhā; it is only a past verb, and when it is a past verb the tamyīz does not come with it, and its passing [as transitive] to أمدا is clearer and more evident. If you make أمدا accusative by لبثوا, it is an adverb, but it obliges you to have made أحصى transitive with a preposition, because the implied form would be "reckoned their tarrying in the term", while it is among the verbs that do not need a preposition; so that is somewhat far-fetched, and making it accusative by أحصى is more fitting and stronger.
As for His saying {لنعلم أَي الحزبين} and His saying {فَلْينْظر أَيهَا أزكى}: the nominative in these, according to most grammarians, is as mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows it is the khabar (predicate), and the verb is suspended (muʿallaq), not governing in wording. Sībawayh's reason for that is that, when the pronoun referring back to أيّ is omitted, it was made indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma. We will mention the explanation of the disagreement about أيّ in [Sūrat] Maryam.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying {شططا}: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "an outrageous saying (قولا شططا)"; it is also permissible that the verb of saying makes it accusative.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {وَإِذ اعتزلتموهم}: i.e. "and remember when you withdrew from them".

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {ذَات الْيَمين} and {ذَات الشمَال}: two adverbs (ẓarf).

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {فِرَارًا} and {رعْبًا}: both are accusative as tamyīz (specification).

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, the Exalted, {قيمًا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the Book.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying {إِذْ يتنازعون}: the governor of إذ is ليعلموا.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying {ثَلَاثَة}: i.e. "they are three", and likewise what follows it, five and seven.
His saying {وثامنهم كلبهم}: the wāw was brought here only to indicate the completion of the story and the end of what is related about them. Had it been brought with "fourth" and "sixth", it would have been permissible, and had it been dropped from "eighth", it would have been permissible, because the referring pronoun suffices in place of the wāw: you say رَأَيْت عمرا وَأَبوهُ جَالس ("I saw ʿAmr while his father was sitting"), and if you wish you drop the wāw, because of the hāʾ referring to ʿAmr. Had you said رَأَيْت عمرا وَبكر جَالس ("I saw ʿAmr while Bakr was sitting"), dropping the wāw would not be permissible, since there is no referent returning to ʿAmr. This wāw is called the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstance), and it is called the wāw of commencement (ibtidāʾ), and it is called the wāw of إذ, i.e. it means إذ; from it is His saying, the Exalted, ولطائفة قد أهمتهم أنفسهم.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t:
His saying {ثَلَاث مائَة سِنِين}: whoever gives nunation to مائة considered annexation to a plural far-fetched, because the basic rule of this number is to be annexed to a singular that makes its genus clear, as in عِنْدِي مائَة دِرْهَم ("I have a hundred dirhams") and مائة ثوب; so he gave nunation to مائة since a plural follows it, and made سنين accusative as a badal (substitute) from ثلاث. Al-Zajjāj said سنين is in the position of accusative as an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to ثلاث. It has also been said it is in the position of genitive as a badal from مائة, because it is in the meaning of مئين (hundreds).
Whoever does not give nunation annexes مائة to سنين, and this is the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī: they annexed it to the plural as they do to the singular. That was permissible for them because, when they annex it to a singular and say ثلثمِائة سنة, سنة means سنين, without disagreement about that; so they construed the speech according to its meaning. It is good in analogy, rare in usage, because the singular is lighter than the plural; it is far-fetched only in terms of the rarity of usage — otherwise it is the original.
His saying {وازدادوا تسعا}: تسعا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ازدادوا, not an adverb; its implied form is "and they added the tarrying of nine years". زاد is originally a verb that takes two objects; Allah, exalted be His mention, said وزدناهم هدى; but when faʿala turned into iftaʿala, it lost [some] transitivity and takes one object. The original of the first dāl in ازدادوا is the tāʾ of iftiʿāl, its origin being ازتيدوا: the yāʾ was turned into alif because it was vowelled and preceded by fatḥa, and the tāʾ was replaced by a dāl so that it would be voiced (jahr) like the dāl after it and the zāy before it. The dāl was more fitting for that because it is from the articulation point of the tāʾ, so the work of the tongue is from one place in articulation and voicing.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying {إِن الَّذين آمنُوا وَعمِلُوا الصَّالِحَات إِنَّا لَا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا}: the khabar (predicate) of the first إنّ is أُولَئِكَ لَهُم جنَّات. It has also been said its khabar is إِنَّا لَا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا, because its meaning is "We do not let their reward be lost". It has also been said the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "those who believe and do righteous deeds — Allah will recompense them for their deeds", indicated by His saying إِنَّا لَا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying {من سندس}: it is a plural whose singular is سندسة. The singular of العبقري is عبقرية, and it is attributed to ʿAbqar; the singular of الرفرف is رفرفة, and the singular of الأرائك is أريكة.

mekki-muskil:39-39.t:
His saying {قلت مَا شَاءَ الله}: مَا is an incomplete noun (requiring a ṣila) meaning الذي, in the position of nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ (subject); its implied form is "you said: the matter is what Allah willed", i.e. what Allah willed it, then the hāʾ was omitted from the ṣila. It has also been said that مَا is conditional, a complete noun, with شاء in the place of يشاء and the answer omitted; its implied form is "you said: whatever Allah wills will be", and there is no implied hāʾ in this aspect, because مَا, when it is conditional or interrogative, is a complete noun that needs neither a ṣila nor a referent from a ṣila.
His saying {إِن ترن أَنا أقل}: أنا is a separating pronoun (faṣl) with no grammatical position, and أقل is the second object of ترني. If you wish, you may make أنا a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first-person pronoun in ترني. In speech the nominative of أقل is permissible: you make أنا a mubtadaʾ and أقل the khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of the second object of ترني.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {غورا}: accusative because it is the khabar (predicate) of أصبح; its implied form is "[water] of sinking (ذَا غور)".

mekki-muskil:42-42.t:
His saying {وأحيط بثمره}: the object whose agent is not named (the deputy agent, nāʾib fāʿil) of أحيط is implied, namely the maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also permissible for بثمره to be in the position of nominative as the object of أحيط [standing in for the agent].
His saying {بثمره}: whoever reads it with two ḍammas (ثُمُره) makes it the plural of ثمرة, like خشبة and خُشُب. It may also be a plural of a plural, as though it were the plural of ثمار, like حمار and حُمُر, with ثمار the plural of ثمرة, like أكمة and إكام. Whoever reads it with two fatḥas (ثَمَره) makes it the plural of ثمرة, like خشبة and خَشَب. Whoever makes the second quiescent and gives ḍamma to the first (ثُمْره) does so for lightness, its origin being two ḍammas.

mekki-muskil:44-44.t:
His saying {هُنَالك الْولَايَة لله الْحق}: whoever puts الحق in the nominative makes الولاية a mubtadaʾ (subject) and هنالك its khabar (predicate), with الحق a naʿt (adjective) of الولاية; the governor of هنالك is the omitted [notion of] stability (istiqrār) in whose place هنالك stands. It is also permissible for لله to be the khabar of الولاية. Whoever puts الحق in the genitive makes it a naʿt of Allah, exalted be His mention, i.e. "for Allah, the Possessor of truth", and treats هنالك as non-governing; then the governor of هنالك is the [notion of] stability in whose place لله stands. Pausing on هنالك is not good in these two aspects. It is also permissible, when you make لله the khabar, for the governor of هنالك to be منتصرا [of the preceding verse], so pausing on هنالك is good on this aspect.
هنالك may be an adverb of time or an adverb of place, and its origin is place: you say "sit there (هُنَالك)", "here (هَاهُنَا)", "there (هُنَاكَ)", and "stay there (أقِم هُنَالك)". The lām in هنالك indicates the remoteness of what is pointed to.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {وَيَوْم نسير الْجبَال}: the governor of يوم is an implied verb, its implied form being "and remember, O Muḥammad, the day We set the mountains in motion". It is not good for the governor to be what precedes it, because the conjunction prevents that.

mekki-muskil:48-48.t: His saying {على رَبك صفا}: [صفا is] accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying {كَبرت كلمة}: كلمة is accusative as an explanation (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz), and in كبرت there is a pronoun as fāʿil (agent); its implied form is "grievous is their saying: Allah has taken a son". Whoever puts كلمة in the nominative makes كبرت mean "is enormous", and implies nothing in it, so the word is nominative as the agent of its verb, and تخرج is a naʿt (adjective) of the word.
His saying {إِن يَقُولُونَ إِلَّا كذبا}: إن means مَا (negation), and كذبا is accusative by the verb of saying.

mekki-muskil:50-50.t: His saying {إِلَّا إِبْلِيس}: accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), according to the doctrine of those who hold that Iblīs was not of the angels. It has also been said it is [an exception] from the first, because he was of the angels.

mekki-muskil:55-55.t:
His saying {وَمَا منع النَّاس أَن يُؤمنُوا}: أن is in the position of accusative as the object of منع.
His saying {إِلَّا أَن تأتيهم}: أن is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of منع.
His saying {الْعَذَاب قبلا}: whoever gives ḍamma to the qāf (قُبُلا) makes it the plural of قبيل, i.e. the torment comes to them group by group, i.e. rank by rank, i.e. in kinds. It has also been said its meaning is one thing after another of a single kind; so it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It has also been said its meaning is "face to face", i.e. it confronts them visibly, from where they see it. Likewise is the meaning in the reading of whoever gives kasra to the qāf (قِبَلا), i.e. it comes to them face to face, i.e. visibly. Abū Zayd related لقِيت فلَانا قِبَلا, ومقابلة, وقُبُلا, وقَبَلا, وقبيلا ("I met so-and-so face to face"), all with one meaning, i.e. visibly and face to face.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying {أسفا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying {زِينَة لَهَا}: the second object of جعلنا, if you take it to mean "We made [it] become"; if you take it to mean "We created", you make زينة accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), because خلقنا takes only one object.
